title: The tape's feed animates background-position every frame of a turn, and no perf scene loads her window
body:
## Summary
While she works, the tape's sprocket edges scroll by animating `background-position-x` on an infinite loop (`apps/desktop/src/companion/companion.css:1538`), a paint every frame for the whole turn; and `pnpm perf:all` has no scene for her window, so nothing measures it.

## Description
`.aw-paper[data-kind="tape"]::before/::after` run `feed 1.4s linear infinite`, whose keyframe moves `background-position-x` (`apps/desktop/src/companion/companion.css:1555`). The overlay's rule and the motion subject's performance-discipline technique allow transform and opacity only in a hot path; a background-position loop repaints its layer every frame. The perf gate's scenes (`apps/desktop/package.json` perf:stage ... perf:mind) are Main's; none mounts `preview.html?surface=athena`, so her window's idle and working cost is unmeasured. Fixed looks like: the strip is a pseudo-element wider by one period (14px) moved by `transform: translateX(-14px)` under the paper's existing mask, and a `perf-companion.drive.mjs` scene (tape fixture, a turn's worth of frames) that the budgets judge. The two box-shadow loops on the same surface are already a recorded owner call (backlog 2026-10-13) and are not part of this card.

## Flow
- a turn runs -> form tape -> `.aw-paper[data-kind=tape]::before/::after` animate `background-position-x` every frame until the turn ends
- build: add `scripts/perf-companion.drive.mjs` over the tape fixture and a `perf:companion` script; record the Before
- move the feed to transform on a widened strip; re-run; seed a background-position loop to see the gate notice it

## Expected impact
A working turn stops repainting the tape's edges every frame (WebView2, on battery). The risk is a visible seam at the strip's end if the widening or mask is off by a pixel, which only the window or a browser shows.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - her tape costs no per-frame paint while she works
Before: 1 infinite loop on a non-compositor property in her sheet (feed); 0 perf scenes load her window
After: unmeasured: needs the perf scene to exist and a browser to judge the seam
Method: simulation - read the keyframes and the perf script list; the perf rung needs a new driver (S-M) and a visual check this round cannot make
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: scripts/perf-companion.drive.mjs over preview.html?surface=athena&fixture=tape, judged by perf-budgets.mjs (frame p95, idle frame requests), on both arms

title: A spoken approve drops the slip with no stamp and no announcement; the voice stamp is unreachable
body:
## Summary
When the person answers a card by voice, the daemon resolves it on the socket and the voice store only removes the card (`apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.ts:299`), so her slip vanishes without the stamp or the sentence a click gets; the `COUNTERSIGNED BY VOICE` stamp (`apps/desktop/src/companion/drawing.tsx:128`) has no dispatcher.

## Description
A click, key or chord dispatches `decide`, and the machine stamps APPROVED or DECLINED, says "Approved. Stamped and sent to the record." and tears the slip (`apps/desktop/src/companion/machine.ts:294-356`). A spoken answer never reaches the machine as a decision: `decision.resolved` filters the card out of the run store, the machine sees `cards` fall with no `decided`, and the slip unmounts. The person who answered by voice gets no confirmation in her window, and a screen reader hears nothing. `git grep 'by: "voice"'` finds only `machine.test.ts:215`: no production path passes `by: "voice"`. Fixed looks like: the voice store reports a user-resolved card (id, choice) and her runtime turns it into the machine's stamp path, or the machine gains a `resolved` event that stamps without sending.

## Flow
- a card waits; the person holds the key and says "approve"
- the daemon resolves it on the voice socket -> `decision.resolved` (by user) -> stores/voice.ts drops the card
- runtime.cardsChanged -> machine `cards` n-1 with no `decided` -> the slip unmounts, no stamp, no `say`
- build: a resolved-by-voice signal from stores/voice.ts to the runtime, and a machine event that plays the stamp with `by: voice`

## Expected impact
A spoken answer is confirmed as a clicked one is, on screen and to a screen reader. The risk is a double stamp when a click and a spoken answer race; the machine's `decided` guard must cover it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every way of answering ends in the same visible and spoken confirmation
Before: 3 of 4 answer paths (click, key, chord) stamp and announce; voice does neither; 0 production dispatches of by: voice
After: unmeasured: needs the voice store's event (stores/voice.ts, another context) and a runtime test
Method: simulation - traced decision.resolved in stores/voice.ts through runtime.cardsChanged to the machine; the first half of the fix is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.ts:296-302 case "decision.resolved": ... cards: s.cards.filter((c) => c.id !== event.id)
$ git grep -n 'by: "voice"' -- apps/desktop/src
apps/desktop/src/companion/machine.test.ts:215 (a test only)
apps/desktop/src/companion/drawing.tsx:128 by === "voice" ? "COUNTERSIGNED BY VOICE"
instrument: a runtime.test.ts case: a card removed with a user-resolved voice verdict plays the stamp with by voice and says the approved sentence; plus a stores/voice.test.ts case that decision.resolved by user emits that verdict

title: Her window re-derives the whole model on every streamed delta: Live subscribes to the entire run store
body:
## Summary
`Live` reads `useRun()` with no selector (`apps/desktop/src/companion/live.tsx:287`), so every run-store write (each transcript delta, each answering flag) re-renders her window and re-runs `selectCompanion`, `toolRows`, `gatedListsOf`, `contractDriftsOf` and the Record's sort over the whole session.

## Description
`selectCompanion` (`apps/desktop/src/companion/model.ts`) rebuilds `groupMessages` over the full transcript and `recordView` sorts every call and decision, and `apps/desktop/src/companion/live.tsx:308-310` recompute the tool rows and drifts, on each store change. A streamed reply writes the transcript once per delta, so the cost grows with the session's length times a reply's deltas (chat-transcript: immutable-model-cached-layout - cost should follow the viewport, not the history). Fixed looks like: narrow selectors with shallow equality and memoised derivations keyed on their inputs.

## Flow
- a reply streams 200 deltas into a session with 300 transcript entries and 80 calls
- each delta -> useRun() subscriber -> Live re-renders -> selectCompanion recomputes groupMessages (300 entries) and recordView (a sort of 80+ rows)
- build: a render-count and ms probe around selectCompanion in a test driving the store; then selectors and memo; re-measure

## Expected impact
Long sessions stay smooth while she streams. The risk is a stale field if a selector misses one the model reads.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one streamed delta costs work proportional to what changed
Before: 1 whole-store subscription; every delta re-runs 5 derivations over the full session (read, not timed)
After: unmeasured: needs the probe
Method: simulation - read live.tsx and the selector; timing needs an instrument this round did not build (an M refactor of the window's one stateful file)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: a vitest probe that streams N deltas into useRun with Live mounted (jsdom) and counts selectCompanion calls and their total ms, on both arms
